notes.headlineMetrics: Headline KPIs reflect the cleaned audit totals supplied for the narrative. Derived charts use direct parsing of the raw Takeout export.
notes.estimation: Search-to-subscription retention is an audit estimate. No playback-speed telemetry is claimed or inferred.

hero.title: Chief Information Aggregator & YouTube Scholar
hero.subtitle: A personal audit of how search, subscriptions, playlists, and comments compound into a learning system that is somehow both strategic and terminally online.
hero.wittyLine: A completely normal amount of YouTube metadata to analyze.

knowledgeMapNote: Seven major surfaces are shown here; the broader audit rolls up 10 distinct domains in total.

taxonomy.label: Gaming and Entertainment
taxonomy.summary: The recreational lane, except it keeps moonlighting as cultural research.
taxonomy.narrative: This is where trailers, anime arcs, internet oddities, and creator rabbit holes behave like a leisure activity with suspiciously strong retention.

taxonomy.label: Full-Stack Engineering
taxonomy.summary: Application architecture, tooling, and the recurring need to interrogate Java in public.
taxonomy.narrative: Searches progress from language-specific questions into systems thinking, front-end tooling, and interview calibration.

examples.label: how to add player in unity

taxonomy.label: Geopolitical Risk Analysis
taxonomy.summary: Wars, state power, and the part of YouTube that quietly turns into an intelligence brief.
taxonomy.narrative: Broad news curiosity hardens into conflict tracking, strategic geography, and the habit of keeping multiple narratives in view.

taxonomy.label: Science and Space
taxonomy.summary: Physics, chemistry, biology, and occasionally the correct amount of rocket content.
taxonomy.narrative: The science lane functions like a calibration tool: concrete mechanisms, strong explainers, and fewer vibes per capita.

examples.label: orb on the movements of the earth too dark to see

taxonomy.label: AI Architecture
taxonomy.summary: From model curiosity to trying to understand the actual plumbing.
taxonomy.narrative: Later-year searches skew toward model behavior, agents, LLM infrastructure, and who is actually building durable leverage.

taxonomy.label: Macroeconomic Theory
taxonomy.summary: Inflation, rates, markets, and the steady suspicion that incentives explain most things.
taxonomy.narrative: This cluster turns finance content into a decision-making tool, not a hobbyist ticker shrine.

examples.label: how to find housing in tempe

taxonomy.label: Philosophy and Psychology
taxonomy.summary: Meaning, cognition, habits, and the occasional attempt to debug the operator.
taxonomy.narrative: This domain reads like maintenance work for the thinking layer: attention, motivation, psychology, and abstract frameworks that still cash out in behavior.

examples.label: man's greatest mission is his journey in search of excitement psychology

annotations.title: Broad curiosity era
annotations.body: Searches are wide, mixed, and gloriously non-committal. The system is still discovering what counts as signal.

annotations.title: Engineering hardens
annotations.body: Technical searches get more deliberate: frameworks, interviews, and actual implementation details instead of vague curiosity.

annotations.title: World events seize bandwidth
annotations.body: Geopolitical and macro searches spike as YouTube quietly turns into a rolling external affairs brief.

annotations.title: AI moves from spectacle to infrastructure
annotations.body: Interest shifts away from generic AI headlines and toward architecture, interfaces, and product leverage.

highlights.label: Late-night window
highlights.note: Still counts as professional development if the tab title says "explainer".

heatmapCaption: Apparently 10 PM is still considered professional development.

rabbitHoles.title: iCapsulate / Shark Tank
rabbitHoles.spark: A startup curiosity query that escalated into founder-theater anthropology.
rabbitHoles.note: This started as one search and became a minor academic commitment.

rabbitHoles.title: Java Developer Interviews
rabbitHoles.spark: Interview prep that quickly turned into observing how engineers perform competence under fluorescent lighting.
rabbitHoles.note: At some point this stopped being prep and became competitive ethnography.

rabbitHoles.title: Mushoku Tensei
rabbitHoles.spark: A single anime search that invited sequels, recaps, and extensive follow-up curiosity.
rabbitHoles.note: A surprising amount of strategic curiosity and anime coexist peacefully here.

channelWatchProxy.note: YouTube Takeout does not expose watched minutes for viewed videos, so this chart uses watch events as the closest credible proxy for time spent.

comments.summary: Comments behave less like vanity metrics and more like lightweight peer review: clarifications, corrections, occasional praise, and a recurring willingness to call weak arguments weak.

closing.title: What this says professionally
closing.summary: The pattern is less "watched a lot of videos" and more "built an ambient research engine." Searches open loops, subscriptions maintain signal, playlists encode priority, and comments pressure-test ideas in public.
bullets: Builds self-directed research systems and turns messy consumer data into a coherent narrative artifact.
Balances technical depth with broad curiosity across software, macro, geopolitics, science, and culture.
Uses lightweight feedback loops to test ideas rather than waiting for formal environments to do it for him.
Can translate personal data into an executive-style briefing without sanding off the personality.
